description: A staffed branch office where the attack begins in the physical world: an implant placed on a meeting-room wall port, reaching corporate file shares and exfiltrating over a cellular path the network egress controls never see. Planted findings: the meeting-room port is unauthenticated because 802.1X was only ever deployed to the staff floor; the print VLAN is routable to the file server and the domain controller; the comms closet is alarmed but its asset audit is quarterly and manual; and the out-of-band cellular path has no control of any kind. Most of the controls that would catch this are not security tools - a visitor escort procedure, a badge report nobody reads daily, CCTV reviewed only on request, and an asset audit performed by hand.

zones.name: Public lobby
zones.description: Walk-in space before the badge line. Visitors wait here unescorted.

zones.name: Staff floor
zones.description: Desks and meeting rooms behind the badge line. Meeting rooms are used by escorted visitors.

zones.name: Communications closet
zones.description: Locked closet holding the branch switch stack and the CCTV recorder.

zones.name: Corporate network
zones.description: Routed corporate services reachable from the branch.

zones.name: Out-of-band carrier
zones.description: Commercial cellular coverage inside the building. Not an estate network and not monitored by it.

components.name: Lobby badge reader
components.description: Controls the door between the lobby and the staff floor. Emits badge grant and deny events.

controls.name: Badge grant and deny alerting
controls.description: Access control server raises an alert on a deny streak or an out-of-hours grant. A real detection source that no SIEM currently ingests.

controls.name: Visitor escort procedure
controls.description: Staff are required to escort visitors past the badge line. A human procedure with no artefact: compliance is not recorded anywhere.

components.name: Access control server
components.description: Holds badge credentials, door events and the visitor register.

controls.name: Monthly badge audit report
controls.description: Facilities reviews grants and terminations monthly. The interval, not the data, is the weakness.

components.name: Meeting room wall port
components.description: Live wall port in a bookable meeting room. Patched to the print VLAN so that visiting sales teams can print.

controls.name: 802.1X port authentication
controls.description: Deployed on the staff floor desks but never extended to meeting rooms, because printers and guest laptops failed to authenticate.

controls.name: Sticky MAC port security
bypass_requirements: clone the MAC of the room's conference phone

components.name: Branch access switch (print VLAN)
components.description: Access switch carrying the print VLAN. Routes to corporate services rather than terminating at a print server.

controls.name: NetFlow export to collector
controls.description: Flow records are exported but retained for seven days and queried only during incidents.

controls.name: Print VLAN egress ACL
controls.description: Intended to restrict the print VLAN to the print server. The rule set was relaxed during a printer migration and never restored.

components.name: Comms closet switch stack
components.description: Core of the branch. Physical access here yields a span port, a free uplink and the CCTV recorder.

controls.name: Door contact alarm
controls.description: Alarms to the facilities desk when the closet door opens outside a change window. Physical detection with no security-tool integration.

controls.name: Quarterly hardware asset audit
controls.description: A technician walks the closet and compares what is racked against an inventory spreadsheet. The only control that would find an implant by looking at it.

controls.name: Key cabinet sign-out
controls.description: Closet key is signed out on paper at the facilities desk. Human process; the record is legible but never reconciled against door alarms.

components.name: CCTV recorder
components.description: Thirty days of footage covering the lobby, the staff floor corridor and the closet door.

controls.name: Footage reviewed on request only
controls.description: Nobody watches. Review happens when an incident is already suspected, which makes this evidence rather than detection.

components.name: Staff workstation
components.description: Managed desktop with endpoint detection. The implant deliberately avoids it.

components.name: Domain controller
components.description: Authenticates branch users and file share access.

components.name: Branch file server
components.description: Branch document shares including lending files and scanned identity documents.

controls.name: File access auditing
controls.description: Object access auditing is enabled on two of eleven shares.

controls.name: Data loss prevention on egress
controls.description: Inspects the corporate internet path only. An implant leaving over cellular never meets it.

components.name: Out-of-band cellular path
components.description: Commercial cellular coverage inside the building. An implant with a SIM reaches the internet without traversing any estate egress point, so no proxy, DLP or firewall sees the traffic.

flows.description: Physical movement, modelled as a flow because it is real reachability: a person who passes the badge line reaches the meeting rooms. Unauthenticated because tailgating and the unenforced escort procedure both defeat the badge check.
Physical movement from the staff floor into the locked communications closet. Authenticated by a key signed out on paper, alarmed by a door contact.
Wall port patched into the print VLAN. Anything plugged in gets an address.
Print VLAN can reach the domain controller because the egress ACL was relaxed.
Same relaxed ACL exposes the branch file shares.
Uplink. A device in the closet sits upstream of the access switch.
Camera streams and recorder management share the closet switch.
Ordinary staff use of the shares. The baseline an implant's reads must be distinguished from.
Not a wired path: an implant on the print VLAN carries its own modem. Collected data leaves the building without passing a single estate egress control.
